title: Evidence refresh, writer perimeter and cost baseline
goal: Turn the sampled architecture map into a complete enabled-writer inventory for the Projects pilot and establish reproducible baseline costs.
changes: Resolve the actual working branch, dirty tree and sibling revisions; remap extracted contracts and hosts.
Trace Projects create/update/delete, children, raw SQL, imports, transfer, seed/test maintenance and every HTTP/tool/UI caller.
Read current testing guidance, complete CI policy, governance journals and canonical migration composition.
Record baseline SQL/rows, lock wait/hold, latency, receipt/projection behavior and UI draft memory with isolated data.
excludes: No application-wide token migration.
No source checkout/reset or change to the developer environment.
No claiming default-branch search results prove the target branch.
entry: Package is accepted as a review starting point, not an implementation mandate.
exit: Every enabled Projects writer is assigned a stable inventory ID and exact symbol/caller evidence; unknown pilot writer count is zero.
Exact owner test discovery is recorded and baseline environment is reproducible.
Decisions D01–D08 have assigned reviewers and pilot defaults are ratified or replaced.
stop: Read-only discovery is useful independently. Existing write risks remain; no new concurrency guarantee is advertised.
risks: Incomplete later-owner mapping remains explicit. Performance baselines may still require a capable local environment, which blocks that gate rather than being labelled passing.

title: Minimal foundation proof and prerequisite repairs
goal: Establish correct transaction/outcome/cleanup behavior and choose only the primitives the first vertical slice needs.
changes: Specify exact edit-stamp semantics, original-value binding, coherent read and child-only root advancement.
Prove source-first lock ordering, nested participation, cancellation/dispose cleanup and commit knowledge on both Projects source paths.
Separate domain conflict, retryable database failure and commit uncertainty in the owner/adapters without replacing unrelated public contracts.
Design/reuse the Projects durable operation result and bounded fact-validation ports; instrument existing gates.
excludes: No blanket removal of local stripes or isolation-level downgrade.
No generic command bus, global mutation DbContext or reflective field patch engine.
No new replay truth duplicating existing owner journals.
entry: P00 complete pilot writer map and measured baseline; actual primitive consumers known.
exit: Two-process and deterministic primitive tests show declared participation/cleanup/commit semantics.
Minimal schema/contract choices and canonical mapping strategy reviewed.
Projection decision D08 and migration/restore identity policy are resolved before P02 implementation starts.
stop: Foundational corrections may ship separately when behavior and guards remain compatible. Project content protection is not yet complete.
risks: Changing a shared utility can affect many owners; named invalidation triggers may require a broader frozen-checkpoint gate before continuing.

title: Projects end-to-end protected edit pilot
goal: Close lost project edits, ambiguous save outcomes and the selected projection consistency gap across every enabled Projects caller.
changes: Add the reviewed content stamp to canonical schema and owner mapping; atomic parent/child/receipt behavior.
Return a coherent editable snapshot and exact accepted stamp plus child identity mapping.
Update ordinary UI hosts, API-only contract, agent tool request/binding and internal callers together; missing/stale preconditions reject.
Implement draft-preserving conflicts, original operation reconciliation and chosen search projection protocol.
Update transfer/import/maintenance token handling and drain unconverted writers; cover delete/recreate and original creation reservation/compensation.
excludes: No full rich-text merge, shared cursors or per-keystroke autosave.
No claim that old planning objectives are now detected by target CAS.
No unconverted legacy endpoint that fills in a current token.
entry: P01 choices and proofs complete; deployable caller/migration perimeter approved.
exit: All enabled pilot write paths enforce original content/lifetime conditions; absent tokens cannot bypass.
Real two-editor and agent-versus-human tests preserve data and drafts; duplicates/lost responses reconcile by owner result.
Chosen projection, import and restore rules pass their actual crash/order tests.
Targeted owner, contracts, UI and browser proofs plus required static gates are recorded on matching source.
stop: Protected Projects edits and their declared projection/outcome guarantees can ship. Other owners and decision-basis freshness remain explicitly outside coverage.
risks: Coarse project revision may cause benign conflicts. Deployment cannot restore old unsafe writers as a performance fallback.

title: Narrow intentions and selective editor reconciliation
goal: Reduce avoidable whole-object conflicts and list churn without weakening the pilot safety rules.
changes: Introduce selected typed add/edit/remove/reorder intentions with their own validated preconditions.
Define duplicate/foreign row-ID rejection, normalization and no-op behavior.
Enable scalar three-way merge only for owner-approved independent fields; keep collection merge explicit.
Preserve submitted/live reconciliation and backend-free rendering boundaries during extraction.
excludes: No universal JSON Patch engine or mandatory field-level revisions.
No silent LLM-generated merge applied as safe.
entry: P02 valid baseline and observed conflict/cost data justify the selected refinement.
exit: Exact intent/collection and third-writer merge races pass.
UI draft survival and public API/tool schema parity remain proven.
Comparison reports whether conflict rate or query/allocation cost actually improved.
stop: Projects becomes more usable; coarse protected save can remain as explicit replace. Fine-grained collaboration remains out of scope.
risks: More commands increase contract surface. Keep only those with a real use case and testable domain meaning.

title: One governed decision-basis and approval pilot
goal: Protect a real planning operation against stale inputs and superseded intent, beyond target-row concurrency.
changes: Bind exact proposal, mandatory Projects/Workbench inputs and set-membership witness to the original runtime invocation.
Validate bounded source basis under actual publication protection using typed owner ports.
Bind approval to the reviewed proposal/basis/authority and reject material drift.
Implement explicit takeover/override semantics for the pilot and reject late retired attempts at the owner.
Bound semantic replans and distinguish them from technical retries/outcome lookup.
excludes: No claim of proof of model reasoning.
No collecting every read in every chat as a dependency.
No platform-wide process/checkpoint migration yet.
entry: P03 supports the required precise intentions; policy owner defines material inputs and takeover scope.
exit: Objective change, phantom task insertion, revoked claim and stale approval tests pass with no partial effects.
Actual governed tool-to-owner roundtrip and a human intervention UI journey are validated.
Replan budget, basis limits and source protection level are documented and measured.
stop: The named planning operation gains source/authority guarantees. Do not extend that claim to unrelated tools or all existing runs.
risks: Missing mandatory facts or false invalidation can undermine the feature. External facts remain pinned observations unless a stronger provider contract exists.

title: Bounded owner adoption waves and structural invariants
goal: Apply proven target/outcome contracts owner by owner, preserving stronger existing semantics and closing graph-level risks separately.
changes: Choose each next owner from refreshed mutation/risk/decoupling inventories; small editors first.
Wave A candidates: Prompts, Collaboration flags/create/replies, Resource metadata—each requires current code audit before selection.
Wave B candidates: CRM/HR, Workspace settings, Provider/Agent configuration, Memory/Plugins/Security administration—retain their established contracts and policies.
Wave C: canonical Workbench tasks, assignments, graph moves/dependencies and bounded multi-owner batches; preserve existing expected state and source ordering.
Add shared vocabulary only after real repetition demonstrates a useful stable boundary.
excludes: No mechanical Version-property rollout across every mapped entity.
No replacement of immutable definitions or append semantics with whole-object saves.
No new UI/backend coupling while contracts move.
entry: P02 experience available; each wave has its own complete selected-writer map. P04 is additionally required for a wave adopting decision-basis behavior.
exit: Each selected owner has independent coverage declaration, tests, compatibility cutover and benchmark comparison.
Structural wave proves membership/cycle/assignment invariants under opposing concurrent writes.
Unconverted owners remain listed, not hidden behind an application-wide completion label.
stop: Each closed owner wave can ship independently; unreviewed waves are not required merely to finish a documentation phase.
risks: P05 is a family of bounded slices, not one giant release. Dependencies on other ongoing refactors must be refreshed at each slice.

title: Storage, external delivery and projection integration
goal: Carry valid intentions and honest outcomes through selected non-SQL boundaries without inventing universal atomicity.
changes: Audit actual storage drivers and existing placement/tool receipts; classify conditional replacement and external-edit support.
Bind external deliveries to proposal/authority and stable provider request identities where supported.
Implement guarded narrow compensation and explicit uncertain-outcome recovery.
Add durable projection/outbox work only for selected proven needs; define ordering, backlog, retention and deletion tombstones.
excludes: No general distributed transaction or exactly-once guarantee.
No external network/byte work inside a retriable database transaction.
entry: P04 semantics and the relevant P05 owner slice complete; other unrelated P05 waves need not block. Provider capabilities verified.
exit: Driver/provider-specific failure, timeout-after-accept, external-edit and compensation races pass.
Every selected external boundary declares its real guarantee and recovery path.
Backlog/receipt retention and operational limits have measured capacity evidence.
stop: Selected external effects have explicit guarantees. Unsupported external CAS/idempotency remains visible rather than silently emulated.
risks: Remote services may not support sufficient dedupe or lookup. Operator recovery can be a required product outcome, not a hidden retry.

title: Workflow and Process resume/publication integration
goal: Integrate proven basis, approval and effect semantics into the largest long-running execution paths without weakening existing governance.
changes: Map definition versions, prepared launches, checkpoints, approvals, claims and owner effect receipts to the new semantic vocabulary.
Keep immutable execution snapshots valid while revalidating publication into current mutable targets.
Define legacy checkpoint/basis handling, cancellation/takeover fences, replay denials and compensation behavior.
Update process/workflow UI, tool schemas and recovery operator paths together.
excludes: No unrelated rewrite of the process engine or hard worker-isolation project.
No auto-upgrading old approvals by inventing current input provenance.
entry: The smaller real governed pilot and relevant external/owner semantics are proven; Process UI extraction boundaries refreshed.
exit: Resume-after-edit, superseded worker, old denial replay, stale approval and uncertain-effect tests pass through actual runtime boundaries.
Relevant simple workflows/processes run through shipped UI with recorded effect/read-back evidence.
Saved-record compatibility and non-downgrade policy reviewed; mandatory specialized lanes run or explicitly block claimed coverage.
stop: Named workflow/process paths are covered with explicit legacy restrictions; whole runtime safety is not inferred from a small scenario.
risks: Largest integration blast radius; keep changes in reviewed sub-slices and re-run required frozen-checkpoint/platform gates.

title: Consolidation, measured optimization and release closure
goal: Publish an accurate coverage contract with lifecycle/runbook/performance evidence, and optimize only demonstrated overhead.
changes: Reconcile all selected writer inventories, source drift, approved decisions, risks and residual unsupported paths.
Run documented release/merge/frozen-checkpoint canonical suites and named platform/browser/live/provider lanes as required by actual impact.
Complete migration/backup/restore/retention and mixed-version operational rehearsals.
Tune query batching/lock lifetime/payload/revision scope only when measurement and concurrency proofs agree.
Record operator dashboards, alerts, incident recovery and final guarantee scope.
excludes: No marking skipped or unavailable lanes green.
No unsafe feature flag disabling target or authority checks to hit a latency budget.
No claim all unselected modules were migrated.
entry: Selected adoption scope is frozen; all required predecessor slices and evidence are complete.
exit: Current source, tests, evaluated graph and performance reports agree.
Deployment/rollback rehearsal preserves enforced writer boundary and operation evidence.
Remaining risks are specifically accepted with owner and scope; zero undocumented enabled bypasses in advertised coverage.
stop: Release only the explicit validated coverage. Future additions enter P00-style refresh, not automatic expansion of claims.
risks: Branch drift and long replay/retention horizons continue after release; periodic reviews follow change triggers, not assumptions.
